body:
Asked claude code to review my .aab and gradle.build with this result:

The configuration looks correct:
Export templates (AAR) include libgodot_android.so for all architectures ✓
The AAB file (Halmgaard.aab) contains the library for arm64-v8a and armeabi-v7a ✓
export_presets.cfg has the correct architectures enabled ✓
build.gradle is correctly configured ✓

Likely cause
Since the AAB file actually contains native libraries, the crash points to a Play Store–related issue:
Previous upload without libs – If you previously uploaded a version without native libraries, the Play Store may still be serving it to some users (caching).
Split APK installation – The Play Store delivers separate APKs for different architectures. Sometimes the native library split fails to install correctly.
Testing track vs production – If you are testing via an internal testing track, there may be an older build still active there.

Recommended actions
Verify in Play Console – Check the App Bundle Explorer for version 102 and confirm that the native libraries are included.
Uninstall and reinstall – Ask the user who experienced the crash to completely uninstall the app and reinstall it.
Roll out a new version – Bump the version/code to 103 and upload a new AAB to force a clean installation.

Nothing important really i guess

Hmm do you have an MRP? Would help to confirm this error.

I know selecting mulitple architectures in android exports (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/111407) cause issue by having multiple ZIP entries with the same name but this issue seems to be the opposite problem as it seems to be missing.

On the claude code comment, I'm not sure your setup but try to follow the suggestions, it could just be a caching issue or something on PlayStore's end.

Ultimately, try to provide a MRP and I'd be happy to also look at the issue!

> java.lang.UnsatisfiedLinkError library "libgodot_android.so" not found

I just encountered and solved `"libgodot_android.so" not found` issue.

Whenever bumping a Godot version, you have to refresh/bump the `godot export template`. 

And the export templates have to be built for *each* target (release/debug) and each arch (arm32, arm64, x86_64).

For example, for Android platform, I solved this way:
```
scons platform=android target=template_release arch=arm32
scons platform=android target=template_release arch=arm64
scons platform=android target=template_release arch=x86_64
scons platform=android target=template_debug arch=arm32
scons platform=android target=template_debug arch=arm64
scons platform=android target=template_debug arch=x86_64 generate_android_binaries=yes
```

When extracting the `apk` file (unzip project-name.apk). It should have a "lib" directory listing all archs (arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86_64) containing "libgodot_android.so". Such as: `${apk-extracted}/lib/x86_64/libgodot_android.so`
"libgodot_android.so" has to exist in `${apk-extracted}/lib/${arch}/libgodot_android.so`

Also notice that you are missing `x86_64` arch from your description. Is there any chance that the failing devices are `x86_64`? Some Android devices are `x86_64`.
@grusad did you disable support for x86_64 devices for your app? If not that's likely the source of the crashes you're seeing.
